wiki_only_topics.topic: Herodotus's accounts of Indian tribes and their customs
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: In book 3 (3.89-97), Herodotus gives some account of the peoples of India; he describes them as being very diverse, and makes reference to their dietary habits, some eating raw fish, others eating raw meat, and yet others practising vegetarianism.

wiki_only_topics.topic: Eratosthenes' recognition of India as a peninsula and postulation of Taprobane
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: By the 3rd century BC, Eratosthenes recognised "India" as terminating in a peninsula (reflecting a first grasp of the geography of the Indian subcontinent). Eratosthenes was also the first Greek author to postulate an island Taprobane at the far south of India, later becoming a name of Sri Lanka.
In book 7 (7.65,70,86,187) and in 8.113 Herodotus describes the Indian infantry and cavalry employed in Xerxes ' army.
